newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Afghan minister says government not giving up.
newsitem.headline: Afghan minister says government not giving up.

text.p: Afghanistan's government, ousted from the capital of Kabul by radical Islamic militia, on Friday called on the world not to recognize any regime the rebels would create.

Adbul Rahim Ghafoorzai, Afghanistan's deputy foreign minister, said President Burhanuddin Rabbani and his advisors had retreated to the north of Kabul to Parwan and Kapisa provinces and were contemplating their next political or military move.

Blaming Pakistan for supporting the Taleban, Rahim Ghafoorzai read a statement from President Burhanuddin Rabbani saying that "the Islamic State of Afghanistan declares that any administration to be announced by this group, dependent on the outside, will have no legal or Shari'a (Islamic Law) credibility and therefore, will be rejected by the Afghan Nation."
He maintained the government still had the capability of mounting a military attack but would not do so in the capital where too many civilian lives were at stake.

The Taleban controls more than half the central Asian country, which has been the scene of continual fighting between various Moslem and ethnic groups since Soviet troops supporting a communist government withdrew in 1989.
Emerging from the obscurity of religious schools in Pakistan two years ago, the group has been fighting to oust Rabbani's coalition government and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.
